season.evidence: Stored Jul-Oct. Web search (Mountaineers Tower/Golden Horn pages, WTA, trip blogs): snow-free approach July onward, larch color late Sep-early Oct, early-Oct snow still passable. Histogram of all ascents peaks Jul-Oct (Sep highest).

track.why: Oct 5 2026, summited, starts at the Rainy Pass trailhead (341 m from our pin), camps at Snowy Lakes, tops out on Golden Horn (4 m from our pin). Report: scree up from Snowy Lakes to the ridge, around to the summit block, two or three low-5th moves, rap station on top, scree descent back to the lakes; that is this route (the other three stored routes are multi-pitch technical lines and this party carried a 30 m rope only for the short rappel). Logged route is blank, so identity rests on the description. The track does not return to the trailhead (ends at camp), so it is a trailhead-to-summit one-way.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Jul 12 2025 logged SE Ridge; same scree-to-ridge, wrap to the back of the block, rap ring; but it starts and ends at Snowy Lakes camp (no approach). Backup for the summit section.

facts.text: Mosquitoes are thick around Snowy Lakes in July; bring head netting or bug-free slabs to rest on.
Early October storms can plaster the summit slab with snow, leaving the final low-5th moves wet and unprotectable.
The south summit block's rappel anchor has been a single worn webbing loop; carry your own cord and back it up (Oct 2026).
The upper block has two nearly equal summits; the north one is reached from the ridge side and the south one needs slabby moves from the notch between them.
Short rope (20-30 m) for the quick rappel; a couple of cams for the final blocks (Jul-Oct)
In early October, camps at Snowy Lakes are quiet midweek but larch weekends bring crowds, and fresh snow can already cover the north side of the summit block.

notes: IMPORTANT: ten of the thirteen harvested 'Golden Horn' tracks do NOT end on Golden Horn. Their highest point is 48.5886,-120.7040, which is Tower Mountain (8,444 ft), 2.7 km southeast; they are Tower/Golden Horn combo tracks attached to the Golden Horn ascent. Our Summit pin (48.60368,-120.732189) agrees with Peakbagger and with TopoQuest/Wikipedia (48.60348,-120.73205 / 48.6034769,-120.7327018), so it is correct; no pin move. Only five tracks truly top out on Golden Horn (3376784, 3371772, 2903601, 2417023, 1897401). No complete trailhead round trip on the standard line exists among them. Trailhead pin at Rainy Pass is fine (tracks start 170-340 m from it).
